identity.name: Monaco Chronograph Calibre 11
identity.one_liner: TAG Heuer's blue-dial automatic reissue of the square chronograph Steve McQueen wore in Le Mans (1971), since discontinued.

provenance_events.description: The Heuer Monaco Steve McQueen gave to his Le Mans mechanic Haig Alltounian, caseback engraved "To Haig / Le Mans 1970," sells at Phillips New York for $2,208,000 including buyer's premium — a record for any Heuer or TAG Heuer chronograph at auction.

Jack Heuer designs the Monaco in 1969 — the first square-cased, water-resistant automatic chronograph. Steve McQueen wears it in Le Mans (1971), turning the Monaco into TAG Heuer's most-photographed vintage reference. Reissued 1998, 2003, 2009, 2015; the Calibre 11 reissue (CAW211P) runs 2015-2023.

narrative.story: Heuer introduced the Monaco in 1969 as one of the first automatic chronographs, built around a square case with the crown on the left side. Steve McQueen wore a blue-dial Heuer Monaco on-screen as racing driver Michael Delaney in the 1971 film Le Mans, and the model he later gave his personal mechanic sold at Phillips in December 2020 for $2,208,000, a record for the brand at auction. TAG Heuer's modern Calibre 11 reissue, ref. CAW211P, revived the blue dial and left-side crown on a 39mm case before being discontinued.
narrative.collector_notes: The 39mm case reads small next to contemporary chronographs, and the left-side crown takes some adjustment; check which Calibre 11-generation dial print (TAG Heuer vs. Heuer branding, date-window position) matches the specific reference before buying pre-owned.
